    **10+. People of the land** (decided 21 October 2026). Each province's people in three groups, settled (with its men of fighting age counted apart), under arms and loose, with the flows between them ("People of the land"). Yield and levies come from the settled; battles, sieges, famine and plague count the dead and the runaways; births let a province recover slowly; disbanded men walk home, can be settled as colonists, and turn loose when disbanded far away; settled people move between neighbouring provinces of their kingdom towards room to spare, taking their share of the purse with them once item 9+a has purses ("Money moves with people"), refugees, and runaways from crushing taxes or hunger, cross borders as loose men, a king may settle newcomers in a province with room or return runaways under a tablet, and the loose drift freely ("Where people go" under "People of the land"); a conqueror may deport settled people from a province he has taken to one of his own ("Deportation"), and a besieged king may put out of the city the mouths that cannot fight ("People are worth having, not free to keep"); and the bands and banditry of item 11 draw on the loose, unpoliced loose men robbing a share of a province's purse and stores each season ("Bandits rob the purse"). The king's tax rate moves here from 9+a, so the lever comes with its consequence ("How a king lives"), and hunger answers in the season it bites: a hungry province loses some of its people that same season, to flight first, so the land's worth falls at once rather than a year later ("The wealth of a realm" under Victory). Yield then changes during a game, so scoring, levies and the script kings' calculations follow it, with the benchmarks recorded before and after. Each province's capacity comes from its land and climate, calibrated so that it starts at today's yield, and drought and flood follow its water, with one flood a year for each river shared along its course ("Land and climate" and "Rivers"); and the seasons by each province's climate, so levies at sowing and harvest cost more and armies abroad in a hard winter pay supplies ("Seasons"). In the pace rule, this item turns on water in arid land, fodder and the season on land ("What sets a company's pace"). First guesses, tuned in item 18. Built after item 10 and before item 11.

    **Built in two parts** (decided 21 October 2026), each its own pull request with its own stop for review, since the item has grown into two items' worth:
    - **10+a. People at home.** The three groups and the flows between them, births, disbanded men walking home or settled as colonists, settled people moving within their kingdom with their share of the purse, and the loose drifting; capacity from land and climate, drought, flood and rivers, and the seasons; the pace factors for water, fodder and the season; the king's tax rate, with hunger answering in the season it bites; every use of men drawing on the men of fighting age, at a cost that follows the season ("Settled" under "People of the land"); and yield changing during a game, with the benchmarks recorded before and after. With the men of fighting age come the people who defend their land ("The people defend their land"), and the loose men's numbers following what the roads pay against what the land does ("Bandits rob the purse"). **Stop for review.**
    - **10+b. People across borders and in kings' hands.** Refugees and runaways crossing borders as loose men; settling newcomers and returning runaways under a tablet; deportation; putting the mouths that cannot fight out of a besieged city; and unpoliced loose men robbing a province's purse and stores. Built after 10+a. **Stop for review.**
